To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a patient with slowly progressing anarthria shows preserved phonological effects with auditory input, but not with visual input.

(1) the patient showed preserved auditory phonological processing, (2) she had an impaired visual phonological processing, and (3) the patient was able to improve her visual short term memory performance under unattended speech interference.
The patient was unable to perform phonologically-based processing on visually presented verbal material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of phonological recoded material in visual verbal processing.
a deficit in phonological recoding that prevents visual verbal material to enter the phonological short term store.
the question of how the auditory and visual input systems are connected to a central phonological store.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this patient has an impaired phonological recoding mechanism, which is specific for visually presented verbal material.
phonological recoding is a necessary process for visual verbal material to be stored in the phonological STIS.
the deficit in the present patient is in the phonological recoding of visual verbal material, which, as a result, is unable to access the phonological STIS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phonological STI is not only a phonological store, but also a phonological recoding store.
phonological recoding and phonological storage are dissociated.

phonological recoding is an obligatory process that is necessary to transfer visual verbal material into the phonological STIS, which in turn is the only component able to support verbal short term memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when investigating phonological processing in patients with a deficit of speech output, the use of visual input is recommended.
the phonological short term store (STS) is not only a phonological store, as it is usually assumed, but that it is also a visual store.
phonological recoding and the phonological STIS may be functionally independent, with phonological recoding being the only process that conveys visual material to the phonology-based STS.
